capacity_gross_kwh.notes: Battery passport: 123 kWh total energy, 4680 cells x 1,344 (InsideEVs). EPA filing derivation 122.4 kWh (InsideEVs EPA-docs article); iFixit and ArenaEV also 123. Same pack assumed on Dual Motor AWD and Long Range RWD (Green Cars Compare lists 122.4 gross for the Long Range RWD).

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: Estimated: Green Cars Compare states 117 kWh usable for the Long Range RWD; the AWD trims share the 123 kWh 4680 pack. ArenaEV lists 111.9 kWh usable for the Dual Motor AWD (4.5 % lower): sources conflict.

chemistry.notes: Battery passport lists a nickel-cobalt-manganese (NCM) cathode on 4680 cells (InsideEVs).

nominal_voltage_class.notes: 800 V class (battery passport); EPA filing 816 V total pack voltage (InsideEVs EPA-docs article, iFixit 816 V 150 Ah).

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: Notebookcheck says Tesla's Trip Planner warms the battery before a Supercharger and names the Cybertruck only in passing (as an 800 V, 4680 example); the same software feature runs on the whole Tesla line (Electrek: 2020.24.6 release note for Model S/X). Whether a manual battery-warming control exists is not shown by any page opened (tesla.com manuals 403).

dc_max_kw.notes: Tesla's stated Cybertruck DC spec of 250 kW as relayed on ArenaEV's 2026 Dual Motor AWD page (InsideEVs also: stated spec 250 kW). Higher peaks occur only on a few V4-post trial stations: one owner-posted clip reached 325 kW at 18 % SoC (InsideEVs 2024-08-05; Green Cars Compare lists 325 kW). iFixit lists up to 350 kW at 800 V.

ac_max_kw.notes: iFixit teardown spec: AC onboard charger 11.5 kW at 240 V, 48 A; Green Cars Compare lists 11.5 kW for the Long Range RWD too.
